issues.legal_issue: A quasi-permanent allotment of evacuee agricultural land does not create property protected by the right to acquire, hold and dispose of property.
material_facts: The land was allotted to displaced landholders under a statutory scheme, while ultimate ownership remained with the evacuees.
The allotment was subject to resumption or cancellation for administrative purposes.
The allottees could not ordinarily sell, mortgage, gift or bequeath their allotment rights, and they had not obtained permanent title documents for the land.
issues.conclusion: The interest created by a quasi-permanent allotment was not property protected by Article 19(1)(f).
issues.legal_principle: For Article 19(1)(f) of the Constitution, property must be capable of acquisition and disposal. An interest granted by statute to a specified class, which an ordinary citizen cannot acquire in normal ways and which the allottee cannot dispose of in normal ways, does not meet that test. The Court relied on the statutory nature and provisional, resumable character of the allotment; it did not rely on an earlier case for this conclusion.

rule.if: constitutional_property_petition and quasi_permanent_land_allotment and allotment_subject_to_resumption and allottee_cannot_normally_transfer_interest

predicates.constitutional_property_petition: A person brought a constitutional proceeding seeking protection of an interest in property.
predicates.quasi_permanent_land_allotment: A statutory scheme granted a person provisional use and occupation of land on a quasi-permanent basis.
predicates.allotment_subject_to_resumption: The grant made the person's continued interest in the land subject to resumption or cancellation.
predicates.allottee_cannot_normally_transfer_intere: The person holding the allotment could not ordinarily transfer it by sale, mortgage, gift or will.

issues.definition: When a constitutional property petition concerns a quasi-permanent land allotment that can be resumed and cannot ordinarily be transferred by its holder, the allotment interest is not protected as property under the right to acquire, hold and dispose.

issues.legal_issue: Cancellation of a quasi-permanent allotment under the law that created it does not deprive the allottee of property without authority of law.
material_facts: The allotments were made under a statutory scheme that made them subject to cancellation or resumption.
The Custodian cancelled the allotments while readjusting land allotments, and the cancellation was affirmed on revision after the parties were heard.
The cancellation was made by the authorities exercising statutory powers, rather than by an usurpation of jurisdiction.
issues.conclusion: The cancellation did not violate Article 31(1), because it enforced a power of resumption or cancellation that was an incident of the allotment and was exercised under the law governing it.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31(1) of the Constitution required deprivation to be without authority of law before it could be infringed; deprivation alone was insufficient. The Court treated cancellation as the exercise of a power inherent in the statutory allotment, under section 12 of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950. It also noted that sections 28 and 46 of that Act barred the challenged orders from being called into question in the manner attempted, absent an illegal usurpation of jurisdiction. The Court referred to State of West Bengal v. Subodh Gopal Bose for a broader view of property under Article 31(1), but that view was not shared by the other members of the Court and did not alter the result.

rule.if: constitutional_property_petition and statutory_land_allotment and allotment_subject_to_resumption and custodian_cancelled_under_statutory_authority and no_jurisdictional_usurpation

predicates.constitutional_property_petition: A person brought a constitutional proceeding alleging deprivation of a property interest.
predicates.statutory_land_allotment: The person held land under an allotment created by statute.
predicates.allotment_subject_to_resumption: The terms governing the allotment made the interest subject to cancellation or resumption.
predicates.custodian_cancelled_under_statutory_auth: The official responsible for administering the allotted property cancelled the allotment by exercising statutory cancellation authority.
predicates.no_jurisdictional_usurpation: The cancellation was not an illegal assumption of power by an authority lacking jurisdiction.

issues.definition: When an allotment created by statute is subject to resumption and the responsible official cancels it under statutory authority without usurping jurisdiction, the cancellation does not amount to deprivation without law.

issues.legal_issue: Cancellation of a quasi-permanent allotment is not an acquisition or requisitioning of property within the protection of Article 31(2).
material_facts: The allottees held a statutory right of use and occupation, while ultimate ownership remained with the evacuees.
The allotment was provisional and subject to cancellation or resumption under the governing scheme.
The challenged cancellation enforced that existing limitation on the allotment rather than transferring ownership of the land to the allottees or acquiring their tenure as ownership.
issues.conclusion: Article 31(2), both before and after its amendment, did not apply to the rights comprising a quasi-permanent allotment.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31(2), as it stood before amendment, used concepts of taking possession and acquisition that were inapt for the limited rights comprising a quasi-permanent allotment. The amended Article 31(2), read with Article 31(2A), contemplated acquisition or requisitioning and taking possession as a result of transfer of ownership or of the right to possession; the allotment interest did not fit that description. The Court considered the possible retrospective effect of the amendment but held that the amended provision was inapplicable as well.

rule.if: constitutional_property_petition and quasi_permanent_land_allotment and allotment_is_limited_tenure and allotment_subject_to_resumption

predicates.constitutional_property_petition: A person brought a constitutional proceeding alleging that an action concerning property triggered a constitutional acquisition protection.
predicates.quasi_permanent_land_allotment: A statutory scheme granted a person provisional use and occupation of land on a quasi-permanent basis.
predicates.allotment_is_limited_tenure: The person's interest was a limited right of use and occupation rather than ownership of the land.
predicates.allotment_subject_to_resumption: The grant made the person's continued interest in the land subject to resumption or cancellation.

issues.definition: When a constitutional property petition concerns cancellation of a limited, resumable land allotment, the cancellation is not an acquisition or requisitioning protected by the property acquisition guarantee.
